draft.how_it_was_derived: Every concept is one of this chapter's own learning goals from its enrichment, in the enrichment's order, stated in the enrichment's words. Nothing here was written by this generator: it matched the goals to the questions the exercise bank can ask, to the techniques that carry them out, and to the mastery checklist that says they are checked.
draft.how_matches_were_made: Matched on shared words. Each sentence is lowercased, stripped of its LaTeX and of the everyday words the whole book uses, and what is left is reduced to a rough stem so 'fractions' and 'fraction' count as one word. A shared word is worth 1 divided by the number of candidates that use it, so a word only one candidate uses decides a match and a word all of them use decides nothing. A total of 1.0 or more is a match. Every match lists the words that produced it.

learning_objectives: Subtract a given number from a larger number.
Round numbers to the nearest thousand.
Multiply and divide whole numbers by 10, 100 and 1 000.
Convert between different units (litres ↔ millilitres, metres ↔ centimetres, hours ↔ minutes).
Express quantities as fractions and simplify them.
Solve word problems involving fractions, ratios and proportional reasoning.
Calculate area and perimeter of rectangles and composite shapes.
Find missing angles in simple geometric diagrams.

said.says: This chapter provides a mixed review of place‑value subtraction, rounding, multiplication and division by powers of ten, fraction and unit conversions, money word problems, ratios, and basic geometry (area, perimeter, angles).
You will subtract thousands from larger whole numbers.
You will round whole numbers to the nearest thousand.
You will multiply and divide by $10$, $100$, and $1{,}000$.
You will change litres, millilitres, metres, centimetres, and time.
You will write parts of amounts as fractions.
You will solve money problems with several steps.
You will use fractions to find used and leftover amounts.
You will share amounts using two-part and three-part ratios.
You will find area, perimeter, and missing angles.
